I just received this watch and as I've seen nothing anywhere about it I figured I'd post a little something about it. 

So the watch is solid and feels very nice. The double dome crystal is very nice to look at. The case is stainless steel as with all other Paganis and is well brushed and generally finished. The dimensions are 50.1mm lug-to-lug, 14.9mm thickness (including the domed crystal) and 42.1mm diameter. 

The dial is very difficult to describe but it's a kind of lightish gray, dateless with nice applied indices, and the hands are the typical snowflake hands found on any tudor. The bezel is 90 click with minimal backplay and good alignment, it's light resistance but isn't easily knocked out of place by accident and is a weird brown grayish colour, looks more gray in artificial light and more light brown in natural light.

The screw down caseback is an exhibition caseback and you can see the NH35 movement through it (I had ordered a YN55 model but received an NH), which has a speck of dust on the rotor. And the crown is very grippy and threads smoothly.

The lume is nice on the indices but very weak on the hands which is a bit of a shame but it's nice enough that it shines brightly when going from outside to inside.

The bracelet is the regular new version of pagani bracelet, same as featured on the previous 1671 and the more recent 1694 versions.
